response.body: # gitea-cli [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT) [![Release](https://raster.shields.io/badge/dynamic/json.svg?label=release&url=https://gitea.com/api/v1/repos/gitea/cli/releases&query=$[0].tag_name)](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/releases) [![Join the chat at https://img.shields.io/discord/322538954119184384.svg](https://img.shields.io/discord/322538954119184384.svg)](https://discord.gg/Gitea) [![GoDoc](https://pkg.go.dev/badge/gitea.dev/cli?status.svg)](https://godoc.org/gitea.dev/cli) ![gitea-cli Release Status](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/actions/workflows/release-nightly.yml/badge.svg) ## The official CLI for Gitea gitea-cli manages repositories, issues, pull requests, releases, and other Gitea resources with explicit commands suitable for local development and CI. The binary is called `gt`. ```sh gt auth login --host https://gitea.example.org --with-token < token-file gt issue list --repo owner/repository gt pr view 123 --repo owner/repository --json number,title,state gt alias set bugs 'issue list --label bug' gt help ``` Scripts and agents get stable machine-readable output: `--json` and `--jq` select fields that gt only ever adds to, and `gt schema` lists them with their types. `--template` formats the same JSON with a Go template, as in `gh`. With `GITEA_CLI_ERROR_FORMAT=json`, a failure is one line of JSON on stderr. `--dry-run` previews the write requests of every command that only changes Gitea, such as `gt pr merge`, without sending them. gt requires Gitea 28 or newer. It keeps its preferences in `config.yml` and its instances and accounts in `hosts.yml`. Run `gt --help` or `gt --help` for supported commands and flags; the full reference, man pages, and shell completions ship in each release's docs archive. Credentials use the operating-system keyring by default; explicitly select `--credential-store file` when private file storage is needed. For CI, supply `GITEA_TOKEN` and its instance through `GITEA_CLI_HOST` or `GITEA_INSTANCE_URL`; environment credentials are never persisted. ## Installation There are different ways to get `gt`: 1. Run the install script. It downloads the binary for your system from dl.gitea.com, verifies its checksum and installs `gt`; `GITEA_CLI_VERSION` and `GITEA_CLI_INSTALL_DIR` choose another version or directory, and the version `nightly` installs the latest build of the main branch. Later, `gt upgrade` upgrades it the same way. On Linux, macOS, FreeBSD or OpenBSD: ```sh curl -fsSL https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/raw/branch/main/scripts/install.sh | sh # the latest nightly build curl -fsSL https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/raw/branch/main/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --nightly ``` On Windows, in PowerShell, which also adds `gt` to your PATH: ```powershell irm https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/raw/branch/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex # the latest nightly build $env:GITEA_CLI_VERSION = 'nightly'; irm https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/raw/branch/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex ``` 2. Use the prebuilt binaries from [dl.gitea.com](https://dl.gitea.com/gitea-cli/) 3. Docker: [gitea-cli at docker hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/gitea/gitea-cli) 4. Homebrew on macOS or Linux: ```sh brew install gitea-cli ``` 5. Arch Linux: install `gitea-cli` from the [extra repository](https://archlinux.org/packages/extra/x86_64/gitea-cli/) with `sudo pacman -S gitea-cli` 6. Linux packages: download the `.deb`, `.rpm`, `.apk` or Arch `.pkg.tar.zst` for your system from the [release](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/releases) and install it with your package manager, for example `sudo apt install ./gitea-cli__amd64.deb`. They include the man pages and shell completions. 7. Install from source: [see *Compilation*](#compilation) ### Log in to Gitea from gt Gitea can use many different authentication schemes, and not every authentication method will work with every Gitea deployment. When you are a Gitea instance administrator you can tweak your settings to fit your use case. For the method that is most likely to work with any Gitea deployment use the following steps: 1. Open your Gitea instance in a web browser 2. Log in to Gitea in your web browser. Any MFA, IDP, or whatever else should be available this way. 3. In your "user settings", generate an application token with at least **user read** permissions. If you want to do anything useful with the token add additional permissions/scopes. 4. Save the token in a private file and run `gt auth login --host https://your-instance --with-token < token-file`. Credentials use the operating-system keyring by default. You should now be logged in to your gitea instance from gt. Alternatively, `gt auth login --host https://your-instance --oauth` authorizes gt in your browser. OAuth may not be available on all Gitea deployments, and needs a browser on the machine running gt. ### Coming from tea gt replaces tea. [Migrating from tea](docs/migrating-from-tea.md) maps tea's commands and flags to gt's. ### Shell completion If you installed from source or the package does not provide the completions with it you can add them yourself with `gt completion ` command. Add the line for your shell to its startup file: ```shell # ~/.bashrc (on macOS, ~/.bash_profile) eval "$(gt completion bash)" # ~/.zshrc, after compinit autoload -U compinit && compinit source <(gt completion zsh) # fish gt completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/gt.fish # PowerShell profile gt completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression ``` The bash script needs the bash-completion package. `gt completion --help` shows the details for each shell. ### Man Page The hidden command `gt man` can be used to generate the `gt` man page. ```shell # for bash or zsh man <(gt man) # for fish man (gt man | psub) # write man page to a file gt man --output-file ./gt.man ``` ### Agent skill An [agent skill](https://agentskills.io) teaches coding agents to drive `gt`: checking CI and reading the logs of failed jobs, turning an issue into a pull request, commenting and reviewing. It replaces [gitea-tea-skill](https://gitea.com/gitea/gitea-tea-skill). Install it with [skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills): ```shell # for the current project npx skills add https://gitea.com/gitea/cli.git --skill gt # for all your projects npx skills add https://gitea.com/gitea/cli.git --skill gt -g # after upgrading gt npx skills update gt ``` ## Compilation Make sure you have a current Go version installed (1.27 or newer). - To compile the source yourself with the recommended flags & tags: ```sh git clone https://gitea.com/gitea/cli.git # or: gt repo clone https://gitea.com/gitea/cli ;) cd cli make ``` Note that GNU Make (gmake on OpenBSD) is required. If you want to install the compiled program you have to execute the following command: ```sh make install ``` This installs the binary into the "bin" folder inside of your GOPATH folder (`go env GOPATH`). It is possible that this folder isn't in your PATH Environment Variable. ## Contributing Fork -> Patch -> Push -> Pull Request - `make test` run unit tests - `make vet` run checks (check the order of imports; preventing failure on CI pipeline beforehand) - `make build` builds the production CLI - `make docs` regenerates references, man pages, and shell completions in `docs/generated` (not committed; built on release) - ... (for other development tasks, check the `Makefile`) **Please** read the [CONTRIBUTING](CONTRIBUTING.md) documentation, it will tell you about internal structures and concepts. ## License This project is under the MIT License. See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for the full license text.
